utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. If the case for hearing could be called, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-05-87/1-T, the Prosecutor versus Vlastimir Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. If the witness, who's parted, could be brought in. While that's happening, could the Chamber mention that on Friday -- sorry, on Wednesday of this week, we've been asked by another Trial Chamber to switch sittings with them because they have a difficulty, and because of that we will sit in the afternoon of Wednesday rather than in the morning. Closed session for the witness's entry, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours, and good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And good afternoon to you, K83.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Last time you were here you were speaking about Todor Jovanovic, who brought Jashar Berisha from the police station to the vicinity of the pizzeria. Did Jashar arrive with Jovanovic willingly or did he appear to be unwilling?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was brought there against his will.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. Now could we move on to the next day. That day, did you see Todor Jovanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you know what he was doing the next day, that's the 27th of March, if anything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On that day, well, since the gasoline station was not working, we went on orders of Commander Repanovic to get Jashar Berisha to come and open the gasoline station.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Which day are you speaking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I cannot remember the exact date, but it's that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The day of the shooting in the pizzeria?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I see. Now if we could move on to the day after that. Did you observe whether or not Jovanovic was involved in any investigations at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you tell us about that? What was he doing the next day, that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On that day, I mean, well, the crime technician took pictures of the corpses and took the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Which corpses were these? Do you know -- let me clarify. Do you know what caused the death of these corpses or what circumstances these people were killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they had been killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Where were these corpses located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they were there by the pizzeria, the road towards Rastane and behind the OSCE house.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No. I'm asking you precisely, K83, which corpses did you see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour. The witness stated where he had gone with the investigation team and where the corpses were. The Prosecutor is trying to get the witness to give him the answer that he wants, and the witness gave a very specific answer already, where he was with the investigation team. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The witness has not said where he was with the investigation team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think, gentlemen, we are being very -- shadow-sparring over something that is not a significant issue, unless I misunderstand things. I will ask a question of the witness which might clarify this and allow us to move on. You're speaking of corpses on the 27th of March. In your evidence on Friday you described the killing of a number of people, two by the OSCE house and others at or in the vicinity of the pizzeria. The corpses that were photographed on the 27th of March, are they the same corpses that had been killed the previous day or are they different bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All the corpses were photographed, and Dr. Boban established that all the corpses were dead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think you are misunderstanding the issue. Maybe I didn't put it clearly enough. We're just wanting to know whether these are the people that you saw killed the previous day or are they different people that were photographed on the 27th of March?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the 27th of March, other people were also photographed, people who weren't by the pizzeria.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The people who were killed on the 26th of March, were they photographed by the crime technician on the 27th of March?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said you saw the people who were killed at the pizzeria, their bodies placed into trucks which were driven away. Do you recall saying that, K83?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Where were they photographed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right there by the pizzeria.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay. Maybe there is some confusion on the dates. Were they photographed on the same day that they were killed or were they photographed on another day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those in front of the pizzeria were photographed on that day, whereas the other ones on the road towards Rastane were photographed on the following day, and they were buried out there in the cemetery, under the codes that were already there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. Now I'd like to focus on those who were photographed on the following day, that is, those who were killed on the road to Rastane, and I think you said there were some others in the vicinity of the OSCE house. Were there corpses in the vicinity of the OSCE house that was photographed the day after the killing at the pizzeria, that is, the 27th of March?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't understand that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I just want to clarify something that I think you might have said. The day after the incident in the pizzeria, some bodies were photographed. Were the bodies that were photographed the day after the killing in the pizzeria inclusive of bodies that were at the vicinity of the OSCE house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Good. Now I'd like to focus on these bodies that were photographed on the 27th, that's the day after the pizzeria incident. Were these persons civilians or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you know the circumstances of how these persons came to be killed? And that's apart from the four that you saw being shot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour. First of all, the witness has to say about what corpses he is talking. It's not for the Prosecutor to infer that these are different corpses in relation to the ones by the OSCE house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We do seem to be getting into some confusion, Mr. Stamp, and Mr. Djurdjic is correctly asking that you not lead the witness about this matter, so that if you could be careful. I don't think that my questioning helped, in reflection, and I think that the witness has it clear in his mind but we are not managing to get from him what it is that is clear in his mind, so if you'd like to spend a little moment trying to clarify what he says about the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said, K83, that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The witness is M83, if I could mention. K?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I have him wrongly noted as M38. We're having a good afternoon, Mr. Stamp. Very well, K.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In respect to the bodies that you saw photographed the next day, the day after the pizzeria killings, in the vicinity of the OSCE house, do you know the circumstances of how those persons came to be killed? Do you understand what I just asked or would you like me to repeat it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't understand that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The bodies that were photographed in the vicinity of the OSCE house, what caused their death or the death of these people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they had been killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you know by whom or what, in what circumstances?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't see everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm asking if you know the circumstances that brought about their deaths.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were killed by gun-fire from a rifle, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you know who shot them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, there were quite a few policemen. I couldn't see everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So based on what you observed, can you help us as to who shot these people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said they were photographed on the 26th. Do you know when they were shot, that is, the date when they were shot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not say exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. Objection, Your Honour. The witness is talking about the 27th and the honourable Prosecutor says that these corpses were photographed on the 26th. I would kindly ask that a precise question be put.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That is correct. I'm referring to their being photographed -- the corpses that were photographed on the 27th.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So may I rephrase the question, K83. Those persons whose bodies were photographed in the vicinity of the OSCE house on the 27th, do you know the day - I'm not asking you for the precise time - but the day when they were shot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the day is the 26th.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, during 1999, that is, the year 1999, and the year 2000, do you know if any of the police involved in these massacres were arrested or charged? I'm only asking you about 1999 and 2000, not what happened after, if anything happened after.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I really could not say exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did Cukaric remain in the police force during the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did Tanovic remain in the police force during the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did Vitosevic and Repanovic, as head of the police station and commander respectively, remain in their posts during the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You mentioned Cegar 1, their commander. Do you know the name of the commander of Cegar 1? Let me rephrase. You saw the Cegar unit that you saw alighting from two armoured vehicles, and you said that Cegar 1 was your commander. Do you know the name of Cegar 1?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mitrovic. Mitrovic, that's his last name. I can't remember his first name. I think it's Rado Mitrovic, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: During the war in 1999, had you ever seen him at the police station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He came often to see the commander, Radojko Repanovic. He came to sort of meetings, discussions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you know if he had an office or do you know where he was posted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know exactly where he was posted, but I know -- well, I saw him often because I was on the commander's security detail. I saw him often. I saw him coming to the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you know if he remained in his position as head of the unit during the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And do you know whether or not he was prosecuted for anything in relation to these killings during 1999 and 2000?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know about 1999 and 2000, but I know that he's detained now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes. There is a case going on now in Serbia in respect to the killings in the pizzeria; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Just one or two areas I'd like to tie up before I sit. You said that -- or perhaps I should ask a more open question. Did Cukaric have any communications equipment with him on the day of the 26th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. He had radio communications equipment, that is to say, two devices, two Motorolas.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And in the course of the events during the 26th, from the time when Cegar 1 told you to get moving to the killings at the pizzeria, did he use those Motorolas?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, he did use them, but he would always move away from us so that we couldn't listen in to what he was saying while he was having those conversations.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In the course of the events of the 26th, during the time-frame that I just mentioned, at what stage did he use the Motorolas?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I have trouble hearing what the interpreters are saying. The sound is not too good.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: During the events leading up to the killing in the pizzeria, at what stage did he use the Motorolas?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, he used it after everything was done, after all those people had been killed in the pizzeria.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'd like to take you back to the time when you, Tanovic, Cukaric, and your other colleague, I think it's Petrovic, were drinking the liquor that you had brought. Did Cukaric at that time or Tanovic say what they intended to do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, as far as I can recall, they didn't make any comments as to what they would do, and I was really surprised when he broke the shop window all of a sudden.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the witness has already answered that question. In fact, he answered it on Friday, so this is asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I don't think that Mr. Stamp can be criticised for unnecessarily going over evidence again at the moment. He is clarifying one or two matters which concern him, as I understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So please continue, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: After Tanovic and Cukaric shot into the pizzeria, did either of them say anything to you in respect to the shooting of these people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, he didn't say anything. He just said that we should take shelter because he would throw a hand-grenade, because of the explosion, lest any of us should be injured.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes. And what I was asking is after the hand-grenades were thrown and the shooting into the pizzeria by both Tanovic and Cukaric, did they ask you to do anything in respect to -- or ask you if you wanted to do anything in respect to the shooting of these people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they asked me if I wanted to take part, but I had known these people and I couldn't do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And the people who were shot in the pizzeria, what ethnicity were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, K83. That is all I have, subject to His Honour. You will probably be asked questions by other parties here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours. That is all I have in-chief, may it please you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stamp. Mr. Djurdjic, do you have cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I will have some questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, my name is Veljko Djurdjic, and I'm a member of Mr. Vlastimir Djordjevic's Defence team. He is the accused in this case. Together with me is Ms. Marie O'Leary, as a team member, and lead counsel Dragoljub Djordjevic is away because he has some work on the case. I would like to go on addressing you as sir. Is that all right with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Since we speak the same language, could I ask you please to speak more slowly and to make a pause before you start giving your answers so that the interpreters are able to interpret both my question and your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Fine, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: If we could perhaps speed up this cross-examination by me asking you questions and you answering briefly with either yes or no, if you can. If you don't understand my question, please let me know and I will either rephrase or state it in more -- in clearer terms. Can we then begin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have Exhibit P269.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Sir, I hope you recognise this picture. Do you see the church and the church tower here, or spire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I can't see it. Rather, you can see the place where it used to be, but we can't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark the location where the church used to be and put number 1 next to it, and if you could also mark the location of the spire and put number 2 next to it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What did you mark with number 1?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The spire.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And number 2, that's the church?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The church and the spire, were they in existence on the 26th of March, 1999?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: When did you leave Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In 1999, it was in June. I don't know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell me, as you were leaving Suva Reka were the church and the spire still there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right if I say that this photograph was taken after you had already left Suva Reka, or after June 1999?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document into evidence and I would like to get a number for it, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D00008, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Sir, you told us that you completed secondary education. Could you please tell us, what kind of secondary school and what is your occupation?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Excuse me. Let us -- I just rise because I'd like to remind counsel and the witness also that in answering they should be careful not to say anything in open session that might disclose his identity. So I really just rise at this point --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I don't think this is likely to, Mr. Stamp. Thank you for your caution. Carry on, please, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you please give us your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I completed secondary school for car electricians.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: We don't have to go into private session, but could you please tell us when you got the job that you did get in the end, what kind of work did you do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I worked in the warehouse where finished goods were stored.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it true that when you joined the reserve force in 1994 of the Suva Reka MUP that you actually completed training for police officers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not complete the training, but we did get some training, some drills, at the Prizren training area and that counted as some kind of training.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it true that when you became active in the reserve force that you were an authorised official and that you acted as a policeman with the assistance of regular-duty police officers who had more experience?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us try to explain the organisation of the police in the Prizren area. Would you agree with me that the Prizren SUP was superior to the OUP Suva Reka, the OUP Dragas, and the Opalje station, and that it took care of internal affairs in the areas of those municipalities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it true that the -- the OUP Suva Reka took care of internal affairs in the area of the municipality of Suva Reka and that it also included the police station, the crime-fighting section, and the general affairs section and administrative affairs section?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it true that the OUP Suva Reka was run by the chief and that the commander was in charge of the police station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right when I say that the commander of the police station in Suva Reka was responsible for his work to the chief of the OUP in Suva Reka and that the chief of the OUP Suva Reka was in turn responsible for his work to the chief of the Prizren SUP?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I think that was the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it true that the same building housed both the Suva Reka OUP and also the State Security Department section for Prizren, which was in the same building but in a separate area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it true that the Suva Reka OUP was part of the Public Security Department and that it had nothing to do with the State Security Department of Prizren?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I'm not --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. Is it true that the -- that Vitosevic, the chief of the OUP Suva Reka, could not issue any orders to the head of the branch office of the State Security Department in Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right when I say that the PJP units, and Cegar's were part of it, were not part of the Suva Reka OUP, did not carry out regular security police work in the Suva Reka area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they did belong -- or, rather, they were assisting the PJP but they were not under the command of the Suva Reka OUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You answered a different question, but what I wanted to ask you is whether they patrolled around Suva Reka, whether they kept watch in Suva Reka. Did they identify and catch criminals in Suva Reka? Did they do beat work?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they were assisting there in Suva Reka.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you please answer my question? Give me a direct answer. Did they do the kind of work that the police did, the police that you were a member of in Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So you went with them to do patrols, patrol duty --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: -- in Suva Reka, to the post office, to the bank?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. We went to Dulje and --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, that's -- I didn't ask you about the hard patrols, as they were known. I was asking you about what beat patrols, securing the police station, regular police duties.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, they were not with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right when I say that the leaders of the PJP were completely separate from the leaders of the Suva Reka OUP?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right when I say that the Cegars were only temporarily housed in Suva Reka, and only at times?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it true that before the 26th of March, 1999, and after the 26th of March, 1999, you never took part in any joint activity with the Cegars or with another PJP unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that on the 26th of March, 1999, in the morning when you took your duty, that no joint activities were anticipated with Cegars; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that on the 26th of March, 1999, as a member of a patrol, in the morning, you received the task to take food, water and ammunition to your colleagues, police officers, who were securing the Prizren-Suva Reka road in the Dzinovce village.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it true that you were surprised when, on your way back to -- from the village of Dzinovce, you got out of the car and you saw two trucks parked in front of the police station and police officers in green camouflage uniform were getting off those trucks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right if I say that you did not know that they would come?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it true that as you were looking at those police officers who had come in and who were moving down the Rastane road, that a jeep arrived from the direction of Prizren, stopped at the place that you marked on the map or, rather, on the photograph, and a person got out and you said that this was Cegar 1.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it true that you did not know and that you were surprised to see Cegar 1 come in front of the Suva Reka OUP at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. We didn't know that. We didn't even assume that he would.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it true that Cegar 1 headed towards you and that the assistants -- the assistant started to salute him, in accordance with the rules?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it true that Cegar 1 started shouting at the assistant?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it true that the assistant was caught by surprise and confused at this conduct by Cegar 1?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it true that Cegar 1 did not order you to go out and kill Albanian civilians as you were standing in front of the OUP Suva Reka, in the street there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it true that Cegar 1 did not order you to burn houses belonging to Albanian civilians as you stood there in the street, in front of the Suva Reka OUP?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it true that Cegar 1 did not order you to evict Albanian civilians from their homes as you stood there in the street, in front of the Suva Reka OUP?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. He didn't issue any orders to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it true that at that critical occasion Cegar did not order you to loot Albanian houses and to rob Albanian civilians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it true that the assistant was quite confused and that he told you, "Okay, move on"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it true that you didn't know what you were supposed to do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. You are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it true that the assistant did not order you to kill Albanian civilians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please look at Exhibit D001-3214. Now I would like you to zoom in this area between the white house and the house that is behind it, to the right. Yes, yes, precisely, this area here. Could you please zoom in a couple of times, this area between the two houses. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it true, sir, that on the 26th of March, as you stood between the Berisha houses, you did not see any tanks, any military vehicles, or any military personnel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Military vehicles and military personnel?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't see any out there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that your answer to my question is yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it true that in the course of the event that you described for us, the 26th of March incidents, around the houses that belonged to the Berisha family, there were no Roma or any other civilians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There weren't any.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it true that on the critical day and at the critical place you did not see Milorad Nisavic, called "Nisavic" by Albanians, at that place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it true that Zoran Petkovic, Miki Petkovic's brother, and Miki Petkovic was with you in the patrol, that he did not belong to the police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it true that on the critical occasion Zoran Petkovic was not with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zoran Petkovic was not with me. I'm sure about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like you to mark on this photograph the location where you stood when the fire started, the gun-fire started, the location where Miki Petkovic stood, where Cukaric stood, where Tanovic stood, and -- well, that's it for now. So if you could mark the spot where you were with number 1.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Number 2, that would be what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Petkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Cukaric. And number 4, that's behind the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please mark the spots where the four Albanians were standing with an X, if you can see that place, the place where they were killed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's behind the white house here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Okay. So you can't see that place. Okay, very well. Thank you. Could you now mark the path that you took, since now we have this image on our screens, as you went to see where the Albanian civilians were heading?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just like -- Your Honours, I would like to tender this document into evidence, and if I could get an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: First we'll receive the original photograph as an exhibit, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The coloured photograph with document ID D001-3214, Your Honours, will be given D00009.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And then the marked photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be D00010, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, now I would like to ask the usher for his assistance. Could we scroll down -- yes. Yes, fine, and -- right. Yes, yes. Let's have this photograph there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, you described to us the path that you had taken --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Or, rather, let's try to zoom in here, the place where the house is, across the road. Could we zoom in on that? No, no, no, no. Up, up, up, up, right, right, right. Yes, yes. Let's try that. Yes, right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you mark the way you went afterwards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here, here, and here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I do apologise. Did you continue moving or did you stop there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I continued moving until I got to the pizzeria.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Sorry, since I don't know -- well, we see that you stopped here and there are some shops down there; right? We can see that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is that where the pizzeria is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not yet. Not yet. The pizzeria is further on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Further on. So it cannot be seen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it continues over here. Do you want me to go on?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask that this photograph be admitted into evidence as well, up to this point that was marked by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's not clear to me, Mr. Djurdjic, why the witness is stopped at this point. Is it because he stopped there or has he just stopped marking? Can we clarify that with the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can, Your Honour, because I don't understand either.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, please, could you mark on this part of the photograph where you went in order to get to the pizzeria. What route was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, this is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I think that on this photograph we have -- well, actually, let's try to zoom out, say, once or twice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We can't do that, I'm afraid. We would lose the marking.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Then I suggest that we admit into evidence the photograph as marked up to this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can I clarify with the witness, Mr. Djurdjic? Can you tell us, where you have stopped marking, is that the location of the pizzeria or is the pizzeria still further on, off the photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The pizzeria cannot be seen on the photograph, but this is the road leading to the pizzeria, practically to the very corner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be D00011, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise, Your Honours. We zoomed in in order to see the road better and that is why we cannot see the entire road that goes to the pizzeria, and that's why I'm asking -- oh, yes, thank you. This is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So now I would like to ask: You see the white gasoline station here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So over there, could we zoom in. No, no, no, not here. There, right. Yes, thank you. Right. A few times, one, two, three. No, let's go back. It's too large now. No, no, can -- yes, yes, thank you, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, Witness, could you -- could you mark the route that you took and can you show us, if you can, where the pizzeria is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the OSCE house to the pizzeria, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: No, from the point where we stopped - I think that you remember that - and then we can go on, or also since we can see the OSCE house, then you can show us from the OSCE house all the way.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask -- well, actually, can the pizzeria be seen here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The pizzeria is here. Here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you put an X there at that point and could you take the line all the way to that X?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that you did not force the Albanian civilians to enter the pizzeria?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that when you got to the pizzeria there were no policemen or other persons there when the Albanian civilians entered the pizzeria?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the Albanian civilians were locked in the pizzeria once you got there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that in front of the pizzeria there weren't any other policemen or other persons, when you arrived in front of the pizzeria together with the members of the patrol - Tanovic, Cukaric, and Miki Petkovic - and after you had been drinking?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you to mark the place where you saw two wounded civilians and to mark that with number 1. How about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please mark the place -- oh, no, actually you've already done that. The cafe, yes, we've marked that with an X. Now, let us ask you -- actually, I think you did say that this was the cafe where you got the drinks.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's right next to this, the --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you place number 2? It doesn't really matter on which side.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'd like to ask you to mark the place where you had that drink, if it is outside location number 2.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What number should I use to mark it?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Number 3.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters cannot hear the witness. He is not speaking into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could you repeat what you just said? The interpreters didn't hear it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I asked what number I should use to mark this place where we were drinking alcohol. Is that what you meant?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. And you've done that and it's marked as number 3.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask Your Honours to admit this into evidence as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be D00012, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like to ask to call up on our screens D001-3114. I think that I made a mistake. Actually, let's try -- I mean, could you zoom in on the white -- again -- right. 3215? No, sorry. Yes, 5. Now, could you zoom in here on the left-hand side where the road is? No, no, no, down, down, down here, right. Yes, down there. Yes, yes, yes. Can we see that? Yes. A bit more, a bit more. Yes. Now we don't see the street. All right. 3215, could we have that one now, please, instead of this image. D001-3215. Could you zoom out, please. The green house here that is parallel to the gasoline station, yes, down there, yes, can we zoom in there. Could we have that enlarged? Yes. One more time. Yes. Thank you, thank you. Excellent.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you see it better now, I mean that pizzeria?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sort of, in part. Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you please now mark the place where the pizzeria is with the number 1.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Please could you mark with an X the place where you were standing when the corpses were being put onto the truck?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you mark the place where the trucks were when the corpses were being put there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What number?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Number 2.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you mark with the number 3 the place where Dr. Boban and Mirko Djordjevic came immediately after this incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me whether they walked there or whether they had some kind of a transportation vehicle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They came by car, but -- but the car was way up here, the parking lot here by the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you mark that place where they had left their car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Number 5, then?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Let's just clarify one thing. Is this the place where they parked when only the two of them came for the first time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right. And the second time when they came, could you mark with the number 6 the place where they parked their car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, that I do not remember, where they parked the second time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you with Mr. -- with Dr. Boban Vuksanovic when he went to pick up the young men that he had brought to the shopping centre to load the bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: How is it that you know what Dr. Boban said to the young men when he asked them to come with him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I didn't go with him. I was there all the time by the kiosk.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, you said that they didn't want to come with Dr. Boban. That's why I'm asking you how you know that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When they arrived on the spot and when they realised what was going on, then they voiced their opposition.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You stated during your direct examination that when all of this was happening on the 26th of March, that Jashar Berisha was locked up at the police station. I would be interested in hearing when and how you found that out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, you know how it was. On that day Jashar was not working at the gasoline station, and we, on orders from Commander Repanovic, went to get him so that he would unlock the gasoline station so that we could get some fuel for official purposes. However, when the shooting started up there, Jashar Berisha was no longer at the gasoline station.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, please listen to me carefully. Listen to what it is that I'm asking you. You gave me an answer that did not really relate to my question. My question was how and when did you find out that Jashar Berisha was locked up at the police station when all of this was happening?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I found out when Todor Jovanovic drove from the direction of the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So may I conclude that you are assuming that he had been brought into custody at the police station when all of this was happening?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Are you sure that he was not at the police station when all of this was happening?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not sure, but I know that he came from the direction of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, my learned friend Mr. Stamp asked you today about the on-site investigation that was carried out after this incident, and I see that over here, although he suggested something to you, you agreed to the date of the 27th of March, 1999. Are you sure of that date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I've said -- well, I mean, I've said a hundred times until now, I do not remember the date exactly, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that you were securing the investigation team from Prizren in the street of Miladin Popovic by -- on the Rastane road where the OSCE house and Vesel Berisha's house, we know that now, and then all the way to the carpentry store on Rastanski road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that during this on-site investigation you and the investigation team were fired at?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that there was a doctor with the investigation team who examined the bodies that had been found?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember the doctor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It wasn't Dr. Boban, it was a doctor from the health centre. I don't know his name. Was he with the investigation team maybe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, that was Slobodan Andrejevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that you were providing security for the investigation team at the Muslim cemetery as well, where at the individual graves the bodies were buried, the bodies that had been found?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, all the time while that was being done.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now put on the screens, if possible, D -- my colleague Marie O'Leary reminded me that I should first tender this into evidence, and I would like to thank her for reminding me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: First we'll receive the original.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The coloured photograph with document ID D001-3215, Your Honours, will be D00013.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And then the marked copy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be assigned D00014, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we call up on the screens 001-3215.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, we assigned D001-3215 with Exhibit D00013.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, on this photograph can you see the carpentry shop?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I can't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You can't see it here?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we then please -- could I then please have D13. Okay, let's not waste time. It is obvious that we can't see the carpentry shop and the Muslim cemetery on those photographs. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can see the cemetery and the -- on the previous photograph, so I don't know what exactly you had in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It may be Exhibit D10 or D9. Perhaps D9 would be better.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think 9 or 10.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it's a bit further up there, in the direction of Rastane.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have D8.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Please don't make any markings, but could you please tell us, can you see the carpentry shop and the Muslim cemetery here on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You can see the Muslim cemetery and I can't really recall about the carpentry shop. I know that there was a mechanic, some sort of a garage, but I really can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have this photograph, without the markings made by the witness. I think that the clear photograph was number 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I think ...

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I think -- I suspect that that might be in evidence before, P269.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, this is an unmarked photograph. Could you please mark here, you said that you recognised the place where the Muslim cemetery is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark it, then.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What number?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, number 1. We might use it as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you, is the carpentry shop a bit further down the Rastane road, so further down, or perhaps in front, and then you can't orient yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I really cannot recall the carpentry shop.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like to tender this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe it's time for our break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. We will resume at a quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If the witness could be brought in. And while that is happening, the court officer might give us the exhibit number of that last marked exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. That will be D00015, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, will you agree with me if I say that in 1998, in Suva Reka, there were several terrorist attacks carried out in the town, including the assassination attempt on Milan Nisavic who worked in the Suva Reka branch office of the State Security Department. He was seriously wounded. And a shop assistant working at the stall, he was an ethnic Albanian, he was killed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Before we continue, that is a very compound question. It's a question that involves so many composite parts that the answer might be misleading. If the witness accepts that he's correct, it could be misleading in respect of some components.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: My note is the witness appears to have -- I agree with you that it was a number of questions rolled into one. I assume Mr. Djurdjic understood that there would be no dispute about that issue, but do you want to break it up? If not, it will be a matter Mr. Stamp would have to follow up. It might be better for you if you broke up the question now and we were clear about what the witness thinks about each part of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I understand. I just wanted to make things go faster. I didn't want to get a single answer to a compound question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So the first question is -- to cut the question into smaller parts. If I say in 1998, in Suva Reka, in the town itself and in the municipality, there were several terrorist attacks, would I be right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it true that this is why you, as a reservist, was engaged to work in the police station in Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Was that the reason why other police units from Serbia were dispatched to Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it true that this is why PJP units were also dispatched there, including the Cegar unit, as you call it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. That's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that Milorad Nisavic, an employee of the State Security Department, the Prizren section, the Suva Reka branch office, an assassination attempt was carried out in the -- in downtown Suva Reka, he was seriously injured and an ethnic Albanian who worked there at the stall was killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right when I say that from the summer of 1998 until the 13th of June, 1999, the security situation was so complex and difficult that moving around the town of Suva Reka was very risky because of KLA attacks and sniper attacks, and that only those who really had urgent business were moving around?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the police station was fired on on several occasions? By that I mean the OUP in Suva Reka.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were such occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it true that you had to secure the Suva Reka OUP 24 hours a day and that there had to be a watch post on the church spire if an attack occurred on the Suva Reka OUP?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that in 1998, until the beginning of the NATO aggression, the KLA abducted Albanians loyal to the Republic of Serbia on several occasions and abducted persons of other ethnic -- from other ethnic communities, that they stopped vehicles, mistreated the passengers, blocked traffic on main roads, such as the Pristina-Prizren, Pristina-Pec, and Pristina-Djakovica-Prizren roads?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is entirely true.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Was it extremely dangerous to move around the municipality of Suva Reka, in particular towards the villages of Budakovo, Belince, Rastane, Dzinovce and other villages?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't safe.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Was this the reason why the police used armoured vehicles when patrolling, I mean heavy armoured vehicles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did use them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that the police check-points on the roads existed in order to prevent the movement of terrorists, the smuggling of weapons, and to ensure that the traffic could move on smoothly along those roads?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. This was the only way to prevent all of those things, the murders and all the other things that were going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you agree with me that the treatment of all persons at police check-points, regardless of their ethnic background, was the same, that all persons were treated in the same way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have on our screens Exhibit 00003. That's Exhibit D3, without the zeros. I think it was admitted on Friday. It should be a map, a map of Kosovo and Metohija. While we're waiting for the map, we can deal with the textual part. Could we please zoom in to have a better view of the map? Well, we can see the roadmap of Kosovo and Metohija. We can see that roads are marked in red. These are the main roads in Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, Witness, my colleague Mr. Stamp asked you on Friday and you said that from Prizren to Suva Reka it's about 20 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Eighteen to 20 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, from Suva Reka to Pristina, would you agree with me that it's about 60 kilometres?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Fifty-seven.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you be so kind as to mark the road from Suva Reka to Pristina, through Dulje, of course.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you agree with me that in the summer of 1998 the traffic through Dulje was cut off and that you couldn't take this road to get to Pristina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that when this road was cut off, that from Suva Reka you had to go south towards Prizren and then through Sredacka Zupa to Strpce, and then there's a junction with the Skopje-Pristina road near Nerodimlje and then you pass by Urosevac and go to Pristina.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now I would like you to mark Suva Reka and Pristina with two Xs.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And now I would like you to mark with a dotted line the alternative road to Pristina, the one -- the round-about road that was used when the other road was cut off.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We cannot hear the witness when he is not speaking into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think he's talking to himself as he tries to find the roadway.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it's not very visible here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you now just continue on towards Pristina from that point that you reached here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you please go all the way up to Pristina, to this X that you marked here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like to tender this into evidence, and could we please get an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be D00016, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, sir, do you know that on the 17th or the 18th of July, 1998, the KLA occupied Orahovac and that in the course of the pull-out, 60 Serbs were taken away and none returned.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard about it but I was not there in Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you recall that the KLA, on the eve of the NATO aggression, actually killed somebody in Suva Reka and that in that terrorist attack Bogdan Lazic was killed in a shop where you worked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you recall that this was on the 22nd of March, 1999?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't recall the date, but I remember the day when it happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please look at D001-0685, that's the B/C/S version; and D001-0706, that's the English version. Could we please look at page 1 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please tell us what's written in the black letters right in the middle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Criminal Report."

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you see it well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, not really from close up.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Perhaps you could read the first and the second paragraphs in the criminal report here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it's really faint. I can't really see it. Half of the letters are missing and I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm short-sighted. Could I perhaps read this out and then ask the witness if that is correct, because apparently the witness will not be able to read this text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It is now being shown more clearly. I don't know whether the witness is able to follow this. It doesn't look encouraging. Please read, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, I will try and read it. "On the 20th of March, 1999, at around 1430 hours in Suva Reka, in the Cara Dusana Street, number 46," to be more specific in the shop whose name I will not read out, you have it in the translation, "1, the Siptar terrorist carried out a terrorist act, a criminal offence from the Article 125 of the Penal Code of the FRY. The crime was committed in the following manner: The Siptar terrorist entered the shop and at close range they fired a pistol, make unknown, firing several rounds at the owner of the shop, Mate Lazic."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the counsel please slow down when reading because the interpreters do not -- cannot read the text either.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- which is the place of his permanent residence, "literate, married, father of two, salesperson by occupation, of Serbian ethnic background, citizen of the FRY, was in possession of the ID card number 77018, personal ID number 0101-963-954-945, issued by the Suva Reka OUP. He was alone in the shop. He was seated at his desk in the office."

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: The witness could now tell us if I read this correctly. I read the first and the second paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is what I read correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please tender this document into evidence and get an exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. Could we please have also the translation into English admitted into evidence? I apologise, I just wanted to look at page -- at pages 5, 6, and 7 of this document. My apologies. It is due to my inexperience. Could we please first look at page 5. No, no. That is the statement. We need the on-site investigation record, that's pages 5, 6, and 7. And I don't know ...

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The counsel is kindly asked not to knock the microphone on the lectern.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. No, it's not necessary to go on. We have the confirmation from the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be assigned D00017, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. And that will be both the English and the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise to the court officers. It was my mistake. I got confused and I mixed up some of my documents in my notes. I do apologise. Could we please have Defence Exhibit D0001-0785.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting for the document to come up, let me ask you this: Do you remember and is it correct that at Dulje, on the 8th of January, 1999, there was an attack on the patrol from -- of the Suva Reka OUP. They were escorting the OSCE and three police officers were killed, including Milos Stevanovic, a colleague of yours from Suva Reka, and four police officers were seriously wounded, including one of your colleagues from Suva Reka, Nebojsa Andrejevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at the exhibit. Now could we look at the next document, 785.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, will you agree with me that in the middle of this document it says "Criminal Report"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Will you agree with me that it was drafted on the 11th --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Before we proceed ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could I ask if there is a translation for this into one of the languages of the Tribunal; and if there is not, I would object to its use at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My learned colleague, this document has not been translated yet. It was submitted for translation but it has yet to be translated because of the heavy workload. I would like it to be used here, to be marked here, and once it is translated then I will use it as an exhibit, if the Trial Chamber agrees.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It can be marked for identification, Mr. Djurdjic, but it will be a question whether it is possible for Mr. Stamp to re-examine at this stage if he has no translation. Having identified that potential problem, we will mark this document, and if Mr. Stamp has difficulty when it comes to re-examination, he can mention that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, to make things simpler, what I said and what the witness confirmed should be in paragraphs 1 and 2 of the criminal report, and I merely wanted to show him the on-site investigation record and perhaps one more page. But if you think that this will make it more complicated for my friend Mr. Stamp to conduct his redirect, I don't have to even have this document marked for identification, if Mr. Stamp believes that it will make his redirect more difficult.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The problem really is that before we even reach the redirect stage, it's impossible to follow what he's doing, if he selects two paragraphs and reads it or has the witness read it, because I want to see the document in context. And I think that is, to some degree -- well, I wouldn't say "flouting," but the order was that we should be provided the documents 48 hours before, and I think that means that we should be provided the documents in a language of the Tribunal. So efforts have to be made by counsel to have documents which they propose to use in cross-examination translated before the cross-examination. And if they are long documents, then the relevant parts could be translated and I'm prepared to discuss with counsel some agreement in respect to long documents. I don't expect that they will be translated. But generally speaking, we can't follow properly the examination of the witness without having translations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: This, gentlemen, is one of the little problems that arise as we're getting used to the procedure to be followed in the trial. As I see it, Mr. Djurdjic, the witness has agreed that he knows of this event and of the death and the wounding of a number of police officers, as you have indicated. If that matter is not being challenged by Mr. Stamp, you really don't need this written criminal report to confirm that. It's accepted. If Mr. Stamp, when he comes to re-examine, is going to challenge what you've put to the witness, well, then, it may be necessary to adjourn this question until the document can be translated, if the document is going to help us resolve it. But I suspect at the moment that if you don't go further with this document, you have the witness's acceptance that this event occurred and we may not hear anything more about it. For the future, as you will appreciate, and it's clear that you do, the need for a translation in a language that can be followed both by the Chamber and by Mr. Stamp, or whoever is dealing with the matter for the Prosecution, is important, just as it will be important that there always be a B/C/S document, a copy of any English-language document which Mr. Stamp wishes to tender, so that you can follow it and you can decide whether the matter needs to be pursued. Can I take it, then, Mr. Djurdjic, that you do not press the tender of this document at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I withdraw my request to mark this document for identification. Thank you. But I do have this big problem. The documents are long, and to submit them to the translation service, I think it would take a long time for them to be translated and it would all be in vain. That is why I wanted to get the gist of the document and then the service would be able to translate the rest in due time. This document contains 40 pages, plus the photographs, and I think that there's no court in the world that would be able to have such huge documents translated on time. I will strive to use only documents that have already been translated into all the relevant languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If it accords with the witness's recollection of the event, as you've heard from this witness about this event. If you can reach the happy stage where you have a translated document, you, of course, may use it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have learned something now. When the witness confirms something, then we don't need to resort to a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, we mentioned Dr. Boban Vuksanovic here and Mirko Djordjevic. Do you remember that the two of them lost their lives in a terrorist attack on the 17th of April, 1999, by the village of Sopina, on a road there? They were killed by the KLA.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, sir, your superiors at the OUP, in the police station, did they take the measures prescribed by law against the policemen who committed crimes? And are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
